published_results.claim: `static-score-snapshot.json` records how the plugin-eval static layer scores every skill at quick depth.
published_results.metric: plugin-eval static-layer score per skill (static_score 0-1, composite 0-100, badge); sub-scores such as frontmatter_quality, token_efficiency, progressive_disclosure
published_results.value: 183 skill entries in the file (the repo publishes no aggregate). Badges in file: gold 13, silver 100, bronze 65, no_badge 5
published_results.notes: NOT a performance outcome. The repo itself says 'The static layer is a lint' (plugins/plugin-eval/README.md:3-4); sub-scores are heuristics on file structure (line counts, MUST/NEVER density, trigger phrases; docs/plugin-eval.md:152-158). Used as a regression snapshot for the scoring code, not as evidence that skills improve agent results. Excluded from strongest_evidence_type.

published_results.value: OpenCode 191/191 subagents; Copilot 191 agent profiles, 155 skills, 25 commands validated; Pi 105/105 templates and 183/183 skills; gh skill 183/183; npx skills 183/183
published_results.notes: Pass/fail compatibility verification (do the generated files load), not a measured outcome of agent quality. Excluded from strongest_evidence_type.

summary: The repo publishes no measured outcome of its 202 agents / 185 skills (no accuracy, success-rate, token or cost results); evals/README.md:23-27 says the LLM-judge and Monte Carlo layers are unvalidated against human labels and the trace-based eval program is 'in progress' with traces kept outside the repo. What it does commit is a reproducible static-lint score snapshot for 183 skills (make eval-snapshot) and a real-CLI round-trip table showing generated artifacts load in 6+ harnesses (make smoke-test); both are structural checks, not performance evidence (the dimension table at docs/plugin-eval.md:437-442 is an illustrative sample report).
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
